  "text": "No one moved. The bell’s note traveled over the water, fading into the hush between waves.

Then came the second ring.

Elian snatched the lantern from the table. “Cover it.”

Ada threw her coat over the flame. Darkness swallowed the hut, leaving only the compass needle, faintly silver in Peter’s hand. It trembled with each distant toll.

Mara found the door latch. “If we don’t answer, what happens?”

“Nothing,” Elian said, too quickly.

The third ring sounded. The compass jerked toward the door, and Peter felt a tug beneath his ribs, as if a hook had caught there. Beyond the wall, someone called his name.

Not Tomas’s voice. His mother’s.

Peter stumbled back. He had not heard her voice since the winter the sea took her, yet he knew the gentle impatience in it, the way she softened the last syllable.

“Peter, darling. Come outside.”

Mara seized his wrist. “It isn’t her.”

“I know.” But the words came out thin.

Elian pulled a brass key from a chain beneath her collar and shoved it into Ada’s palm. “The boathouse. There’s a skiff hidden under the netting. Take the eastern channel, and don’t look back.”

“What about you?” Peter asked.

“I’ll keep the bell occupied.”

Elian stepped into the dark. The door opened, and cold salt air rushed in. For an instant, Peter saw a figure standing on the shore: tall, dripping, and crowned with strands of weed.

It raised one hand.

The bell rang again, though no tower stood on the island.

Peter closed his fingers around the compass. Its needle pointed toward the boathouse now. Together, the three of them ran."
